$$

$$
(-3)\cdot (\sin \alpha)+\frac{(-3)\cdot (\cos^{2} \alpha)}{\sin \alpha}=\frac{-3}{\sin \alpha}.

question.:question/problem: Simplify the trigonometric expression $\frac{- \frac{2}{3}+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos x)}{\sin x}+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\tan x).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we rewrite the second term using the definition of the quotient ratio. This gives:

$$
\frac{- \frac{2}{3}+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos x)}{\sin x}+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\tan x)=\frac{- \frac{2}{3}+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos x)}{\sin x}+\frac{(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\sin x)}{\cos x}
$$

We put both terms over a common denominator, and combine the two fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{- \frac{2}{3}+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos x)}{\sin x}+\frac{(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\sin x)}{\cos x} & =\frac{(- \frac{2}{3}+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos x))\cdot \cos x}{\sin x\cdot \cos x}+\frac{(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\sin^{2} x)}{\sin x\cdot \cos x} \\  & =\frac{(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos x)+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos^{2} x)+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\sin^{2} x)}{\sin x\cdot \cos x} \\  & =\frac{(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos x)+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot ((\cos^{2} x+\sin^{2} x))}{\sin x\cdot \cos x} \\  & =\frac{(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos x)+(- \frac{2}{3})}{\sin x\cdot \cos x} \\ \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify using the Pythagorean identity $\sin^{2} x+\cos^{2} x=1$. Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{- \frac{2}{3}+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos x)}{\sin x}+(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\tan x)=\frac{(- \frac{2}{3})\cdot (\cos x)+(- \frac{2}{3})}{\sin x\cdot \cos x}.
$$
